transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. This is our week three POC check-in, focused on the Dedicated sizing and autoscale / burst planning. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal here.
[00:09] Sofia Martinez: Sofia. DevOps.
[00:11] Lara Green: Lara, product.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Priya from Redwood, engineering.
[00:16] Alex Chen: Cool. I pulled the metrics from last week's run — we have the dashboard link in the notes, right? (link: /redwood/pocs/NR/week2-run-spreadsheet)
[00:25] Jamal Ortiz: Yep I saw the spreadsheet, looks like peak QPS was about 80 with a p50 at 120 ms and p95 around 680 ms, p99 spiked to 1.8s on longer sequences. Some of that is cold-starts I think.
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: Yup, a few notes: the Dedicated pool we used was configured with min replicas 2, max 8, GPU type A100-40GB in that test. Warmup was only the default 30s, so we saw scale up latencies when a burst arrived. Also KV cache hit-rate was about 42% on average which affected effective token generation time.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: Quick Q — we asked for p4d originally. Are the A100 numbers representative or should we be testing on p4d?
[01:12] Alex Chen: Good catch. Our hosted infra allocated A100s for availability. Performance curves differ but the autoscale behavior is agnostic — kernel throughput will shift but knobs are the same. We'll test p4d in the next run if you can provision quotas.
[01:25] Lara Green: Jamal, is 80 QPS realistic for production? Should we assume burst to 200 QPS?
[01:30] Jamal Ortiz: For peak shopping events, yes — headless checkout flows can get to 180–220 QPS for short bursts, 20–60s windows. Our SLO is p95 < 700 ms.
[01:44] Priya Kapoor: Okay that clarifies. So plan: two autoscale profiles A/B. Profile A conservative: min 2, target buffer 30%, max 6, cooldown 60s, scale step 1. Profile B aggressive: min 2, buffer 60%, max 12, cooldown 20s, scale step 2 — and a burst pool reserve for short spikes.
[02:10] Sofia Martinez: Burst pool reserve? How does that get billed or carved out from Dedicated?
[02:15] Alex Chen: Two options — pre-allocated burst capacity (reserve X GPUs that are idle but paid as part of Dedicated) or autoscale with a higher max and very short cooldowns. We also have a transient burst feature that lets you attach ephemeral capacity from a shared pool for short windows, billed separately. For POC it's easiest to test "max higher + cooldowns" and separately validate reserved warm GPUs.
[02:36] Jamal Ortiz: We don't want to pay for idle GPUs all month. Can we pre-warm containers on burst GPUs only during event windows?
[02:42] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support scheduled pre-warm: you can define windows and Redwood will keep prefix cache primed and spawn containers ahead of expected traffic. That minimizes cold-start p99s.
[02:53] Lara Green: How much does prefix cache warmup help on your end?
[02:56] Priya Kapoor: In our runs, priming the KV/prefix cache improved p95 by ~20–35% depending on prompt overlap. For long sequences it's less dramatic but still helps p99 since generation branches re-use KV.
[03:10] Jamal Ortiz: On the dashboard I saw memory thrash on one host during a spike. Any idea?
[03:14] Priya Kapoor: Likely batch sizing bumps. If batch grows due to queued requests, memory for KV cache + new allocations peaks. We can cap per-replica concurrent requests and tune batching windows. Also quantization profile matters: int8 vs int4 changes memory.
[03:27] Alex Chen: Which brings up another knob — per-model quantization recommendation. For your transformers we're recommending Q4_0 for cost-savings with a small latency delta; Q2 or aggressive quant is not safe for quality. We'll include those profiles in the templates.
[03:42] Sofia Martinez: For autoscale, can we tie it to latency SLO rather than QPS? e.g., scale when p95 exceeds 600 ms?
[03:49] Priya Kapoor: Yes, Redwood's autoscaler supports metric-based triggers — CPU/GPU util, queue length, or custom metrics like p95 latency. We can create a policy: if p95 > 600 ms for 30s, scale out by 2. Conversely scale-in only after cooldown of 90s and sustained low load.
[04:06] Jamal Ortiz: Cool. What's the recommendation on min replicas for consistent latency for us?
[04:10] Priya Kapoor: For your workload and target p95, recommend min replicas set to handle base load (estimate ~2 replicas for 20–30 QPS steady) with a buffer of 1–2 replicas. So min 2 or 3 depending on whether you want headroom.
[04:23] Lara Green: Are there any gotchas with network egress or cross-AZ NVLink when scaling quickly?
[04:28] Alex Chen: If you're cross-AZ, KV cache warmups won't be shared as fast; we recommend colocating pool in same AZ as clients if latency sensitive. Network saturation can cause stalls — check MTU, and if possible keep GPU pools in a single AZ region or enable faster interconnect (NVLink/p4d).
[04:45] Sofia Martinez: We'll check region quotas. I can ask infra for p4d or A100s — we'll aim for A100 first since it's available today.
[04:52] Priya Kapoor: For the upcoming load tests, two concrete configs:
Profile A (Conservative): minReplicas=2; maxReplicas=6; scaleOutStep=1; scaleOutCooldown=60s; trigger: queueLength>X or p95>600ms for 30s.
Profile B (Aggressive + Burst): minReplicas=2; maxReplicas=12; scaleOutStep=2; scaleOutCooldown=20s; burstReserve=2 GPUs scheduled during event; pre-warm windows 2 min before expected surge.
[05:22] Jamal Ortiz: For the pre-warm, can Redwood run a synthetic prompt set to prime KV?
[05:26] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can run a warmup job that replays a representative prompt set at low QPS to populate KV/prefix cache. We'll need the prompt set from you or we can generate one based on your traffic samples.
[05:37] Lara Green: We'll share a subset of logs and sample prompts. Jamal will do that.
[05:41] Jamal Ortiz: I'll export a CSV with request types, seq len distribution; aim to push by Monday.
[05:46] Alex Chen: Great. On monitoring: Priya, can you add per-replica token throughput and cache hit-rate charts?
[05:51] Priya Kapoor: Yep will add those, plus a p95/p99 breakdown per route. Might add a debug window for the next test to capture stack traces on failures.
[06:02] Sofia Martinez: Another question — if we do ephemeral burst from shared pool, how is it billed? Is it per-minute?
[06:08] Alex Chen: It's billed per-minute for the ephemeral GPUs attached plus a small premium. We'll send expected cost estimates under both approach A and B in the follow-up.
[06:16] Lara Green: Is there any risk of noisy neighbor for ephemeral pool?
[06:19] Priya Kapoor: Minimal — ephemeral capacity is isolated at the container level; performance is slightly less predictable than Dedicated pre-allocated GPUs but good for short bursts. For vendor-grade events we recommend reserved burst GPUs.
[06:31] Jamal Ortiz: For the bench next week, can we also exercise longer sequences to see p99 behavior?
[06:35] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely — include 3 buckets: short (<=64 tokens), medium (65–256), long (256–1024). We'll capture latency across buckets and per-token cost.
[06:46] Alex Chen: Okay timeline recap: Sofia to confirm GPU type & quota by Friday (03-15). Jamal to send QPS mix & prompt CSV by Monday (03-17). Alex will send autoscale templates by Friday (03-14). Priya to add dashboard metrics by Monday and setup debug window. Benchmark run scheduled for Tuesday 2025-03-18.
[07:05] Sofia Martinez: Slight correction — Jamal will try to send CSV by Monday but may be Tuesday.
[07:08] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah sorry Monday likely; if not Tuesday morning.
[07:11] Lara Green: Anything else on security/compliance? We still need a quick review of audit logs and KMS behavior for the Dedicated pool.
[07:18] Alex Chen: We'll attach the security checklist: SOC2 controls, KMS integration docs, and audit log retention options. I'll share the docs in the notes.
[07:27] Priya Kapoor: One more technical note — if you enable aggressive scale-out (Profile B) you might see brief transient token duplication in concurrent setups if the client retries. Recommend client-side idempotency keys for generation requests during bursts.
[07:40] Jamal Ortiz: Good call. We have idempotency on the gateway, will make sure it applies to generation calls.
[07:45] Alex Chen: Anything from your side, Sofia?
[07:48] Sofia Martinez: Nope we'll try to get quotas in place today.
[07:51] Lara Green: I want to see the cost delta between reserved burst GPUs and ephemeral — that'll inform our decision.
[07:55] Alex Chen: We'll include cost sensitivity in the follow-up doc. We'll model three scenarios: steady-state with min=2, periodic events with reserved burst, and ephemeral bursts via shared pool.
[08:06] Jamal Ortiz: Are we doing any canary routing? i.e., route x% of traffic to a new model variant while scaling?
[08:11] Priya Kapoor: Redwood supports canary rollouts and traffic splitting. For POC we can route 10% to the quantized variant to validate quality under load. We'll coordinate that during the Tuesday run.
[08:25] Alex Chen: Ok let's recap final decisions: run two autoscale profiles A and B next Tuesday; pre-warm using prompt set Jamal provides; test A100 first, p4d if Sofia can provision; monitor KV/prefix cache hit rates; evaluate cost tradeoffs for reserved vs ephemeral burst.
[08:44] Jamal Ortiz: Sounds good.
[08:46] Lara Green: Thanks everyone.
[08:48] Alex Chen: I'll follow up with the templates, costs, and a precise runbook. Meeting notes and the recording in the doc. Thanks!
[08:55] Priya Kapoor: thanks.
[09:00] (call ends)
